summary: The reviewed implementation supports the claim. It measures median perpendicular contour chords through the endpoint-trimmed, ordered central centerline; preserves unavailable values when insufficient chords exist; converts pixels to micrometres using resolved XY calibration; selects the largest-area width-bearing observed plane for each track; retains explicitly labelled legacy EDT fields; and uses the new representative body-width field in primary tables and reports. Focused synthetic and reporting tests passed. The quantity is an apparent 2D filled-mask width, not anatomical, molecular, deconvolved, or PSF-corrected nuclear diameter.

findings.title: The measurement is an apparent 2D mask chord, not biological ground truth
findings.impact: The numerical width can change with segmentation boundary placement, annotation thickness, focus, lateral PSF, and centerline geometry even when the underlying chromatin is unchanged. It does not establish molecular-scale width, true three-dimensional diameter, chromatin compaction, or a biological mechanism.
evidence: audits/claims_registry.json:99-112 records segmentation, focus, annotation-thickness, and lateral-PSF limitations and explicitly excludes true molecular-scale nucleus width.
audits/evidence/v571_body_width_final/body_width_visual_evidence_manifest.json declares the measurement scope as apparent filled-mask body width and not PSF-corrected chromatin diameter.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:3387-3457 operates exclusively on a 2D filled-mask contour and 2D centerline.
findings.recommendation: Retain the `apparent body-mask width` wording, preserve acquisition matching and calibration provenance, and avoid interpreting group differences as true 3D or molecular diameter without independent optical and biological validation.

limitations: No full image stack or expensive image inference was run, as instructed.

The focused tests cover straight rotated rectangles, tapered endpoints, insufficient centerline samples, representative-plane ordering, missing values, and reporting. They do not exhaustively characterize highly concave masks, holes, self-near curved centerlines, or all pixel-phase offsets.

The implementation assumes a single isotropic lateral XY scale. This is consistent with the recorded Leica calibration evidence, but separate X/Y pixel pitches would require physical-coordinate chord construction rather than a single post-hoc scalar.

The body-width visual evidence was generated at ancestor commit 9cc3ac08250c6216187f5476f65ee8f80a80a305; commit-diff inspection established that the pipeline, profile, generator, and tests did not change between that commit and the reviewed commit.
No other reviewers' conclusions were used. An initial broad search unintentionally returned text from historical review files; that material was disregarded and is not cited here.
recommended_follow_up: Add synthetic tests for strongly curved centerlines, concave or holed masks, border-touching objects, and subpixel pixel-phase shifts to further bound failure modes.

If future microscopy metadata permits unequal X and Y pixel sizes, either reject such calibration explicitly or compute contours, tangents, normals, and chord lengths in calibrated physical coordinates.
Continue reporting missing body width as unavailable and monitor missingness by specimen and morphology category; do not substitute the legacy EDT width.
Do not use this measurement alone to infer true 3D nuclear diameter, molecular chromatin width, or a biological mechanism.
